One PDF per product group, read directly. HUSKY prints TWO rows per measurement, with footnotes quoted verbatim in the PDFs: '*Optimální hodnota představuje velikostní míru na kterou je oblečení Husky ušito. Nejedná se o spodní hranici, ale optimum...' and '**Limitní hodnota představuje horní hranici šíře pro daný obvod části těla, aby se dala uvedená velikost užívat.' So OPTIMÁLNÍ is the measure the garment is cut to and LIMITNÍ is the maximum BODY circumference at which the size is still wearable. Only the LIMITNÍ row is emitted, as body measurements; the OPTIMÁLNÍ (garment) values are listed below rather than mixed in. Row-label assignment: the PDF text flattens, so limit-vs-optimal was assigned from the document's own header reading order (OBVOD HRUDI → LIMITNÍ HODNOTA → OPTIMÁLNÍ HODNOTA → OBVOD PASU) and cross-checked against the footnote semantics (limit = body, optimal = garment, therefore optimal > limit, which holds in every row of every file). OPTIMÁLNÍ values, for reference: women's trousers waist 66/72/78/84/90 and hips 94/100/106/112/118; women's winter filled jackets chest 85/91/97/103/109 and waist 75/81/87/93/99; men's summer unfilled jackets chest 102/108/114/120/126; men's second layers chest 100/106/112/118/124. DELIBERATE OMISSION: the waist row in both MEN'S files extracted as a single series 60/66/72/78/84 — only one of the two expected rows, and identical to the WOMEN'S waist limit row, which is implausible for men's S-XXL. That row could not be assigned with certainty and is therefore dropped rather than guessed; only the men's chest rows are published here. unit 'cm' is published ('v cm' in the headers). [PROVENANCE: numbers come from an unattributed retry run found in the workspace, dated 9 Nov 2026. Three brands from that run were re-checked against their live pages and the numbers matched exactly, but all three claimed body measurements where the page states nothing, so every basis from that run is recorded as unknown.]
